newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION STEPS IN TO SETTLE COACHING ROW.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION STEPS IN TO SETTLE COACHING ROW.

text.p: The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) has stepped in to settle a row between new national coach Carel du Plessis and a provincial coach.

SARFU's management committee told Western Province's Harry Viljoen that he would not be allowed to field Springbok squad members Justin Swart and Percival Montgomery in Sunday's Currie Cup match against Natal.
An angry Viljoen had said he would not release the players for the match.

Du Plessis has allowed three of his 27-man squad to play this weekend to prove their fitness. Japie Mulder and James Dalton are in the Gauteng Lions squad to meet Boland while Mark Andrews should play for Natal.
But Montgomery and Swart will remain with the rest of the squad in Cape Town preparing for next Tuesday's test against Tonga at Newlands.

A SARFU management meeting in Johannesburg on Thursday reiterated that Springbok squad members would not be released for provincial duty until the end of the Tri-Nations series in August unless specifically released by Du Plessis.
In a statement the management committee said: "National interests should be put above provincial interests in all selection processes."
